eligibility: Seminole County FL election worker; registered voter in Seminole County for all positions except Deputy
notes: Verified R4472. Seminole County, FL election worker pay per the official 2026 SOE documents: Deputy $140, VPA $195, VET $195, Asst. Clerk $210, Clerk $270 per Election Day. Election Day runs 6:00 a.m. to ~8:00 p.m. (14 hrs); a half-day in-person training plus an online module are required before each election. Applied as an individual worker, pay is earned personally (the PID organization's pay-donation waiver only applies to the Partners in Democracy variant).

standard.s1: Lane: G40 (U.S. county equivalents 101-200 by 2025 Census estimate). Seminole County, Florida, rank 151, population 491,884.
standard.s2: Election cycle: Florida Primary August 18, 2026; General Election November 3, 2026.
standard.s3: Duties: staff precinct polling places, check in voters, issue ballots, operate voting equipment, assist voters, close out precinct.
standard.s4: Requirements: arrive by 6:00 a.m. Election Day, remain until duties complete (~8:00 p.m.), no personal cell phone use while serving; registered voter in Seminole County required except for Deputy position.
standard.s5: Training: required by law before each election - half-day in-person School of Instruction plus online training module.
standard.s6: Exclusions: not the Partners in Democracy organization variant where pay is donated; individual election worker route earns the pay personally.
standard.s7: Route distinct from other county election-worker routes; no duplicate of existing verified record.

steps: Apply via voteseminole.gov/electionworkers (Election Worker Application) or call 407-708-7711
Complete the half-day in-person training and the online training module
Serve the full Election Day (6:00 a.m. to ~8:00 p.m.) in the assigned position
Receive the position pay ($140 Deputy to $270 Clerk)
